newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BOURSE RESUMES CLIMB, SEEN BULLISH.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BOURSE RESUMES CLIMB, SEEN BULLISH.

text.p: The Athens bourse continued strong gaining 1.41 percent in heavy volume following Monday's 2.02 percent climb with fund managers seeing momentum and expecting stocks to continue to trade above the 1000 level.

"The index was correcting half-way into the session and then it rose again, to end firm. I think this shows that the market has power. I do not predict the index will go lower than 1000 points, in the near future," said George Ventouratos, a fund manager at Aspis Mutual Funds.

He expected the public to diversify out of OTE and construction shares to industrials. He also pointed to Tuesday's strong performance in shares of Aluminium of Greece which rose 4.7 percent on good sectoral prospects.
Other fund managers agreed that the market had a strong upside potential with investor interest keen on blue chips.

"Shares of Titan Cement have rallied and gained another 1.2 percent on Tuesday. Titan has good a good capitalization and positive results," said John Glykos, assistant fund manager at Dorian Mutual Funds.
The Athens general share index closed up 1.41 percent or 14.52 points at 1043.63 from Monday's 1029.11, after opening at 1029.99.
Banks rose 1.23 percent, construction gained 1.31 percent while small caps lost 0.20 percent. Industrials closed 1.55 percent higher while investment shares rose by 0.71 percent.
Tuesday's turnover was 10.2 billion drachmas on volume of 4.3 million shares. Gainers led losers 152 to 60 with 26 issues unchanged on 238 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 840.00-858.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, rose 110 drachmas to 5,135.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $12.71-$13.71. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 5,606-5,958 drachmas. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
